milestones.title: CLI and TUI share one always-on service layer
milestones.goal: The existing always-on CLI no longer owns unique orchestration logic; both CLI and the future TUI mode can use one shared service layer with primitive-oriented snapshot and submission operations.

verification.expect: Targeted shared-service tests pass for snapshot and primitive submission behavior.

verification.command: Review the shared always-on service extraction against SPEC.md and ARCHITECTURE.md and write findings JSON.
verification.expect: Review confirms the CLI/TUI reuse boundary is correct or reports blocking findings with file references.

verification.command: In a temp MU_CODING_AGENT_DIR and temp workspace, exercise the existing `mu always-on` surface after the refactor and verify the visible behavior is unchanged while the implementation now goes through the shared service layer.
verification.expect: The visible CLI always-on surface remains correct while the shared service boundary is in place.

verification.command: Inspect the refactored CLI path and assert it delegates to one shared always-on service instead of duplicating orchestration logic.
verification.expect: One shared service boundary is proven and the append-only ledger domain remains authoritative.

milestones.notes: Do not close this milestone until reuse is real in code rather than implied by prose.

milestones.title: `/always-on` is a real built-in TUI mode
milestones.goal: The TUI has an explicit always-on mode with visible composer state, clean mode entry/exit behavior, and no reliance on extension-indicator string parsing.

verification.expect: Targeted TUI tests pass for `/always-on` registration, mode entry/exit, and visible composer/meta state.

verification.command: Review the TUI mode-state implementation against SPEC.md and ARCHITECTURE.md and write findings JSON.
verification.expect: Review confirms there is explicit mode state and no heuristic string parsing dependency, or reports blocking findings with file references.

verification.command: Launch the real TUI in a temp workspace, open the slash palette, enter `/always-on`, observe the visible mode treatment, then exit the mode and confirm the normal chat surface returns.
verification.expect: The real terminal surface makes the mode boundary legible and reversible.

verification.command: Assert from the renderer state that always-on mode is represented explicitly rather than inferred from extension-indicator labels.
verification.expect: The implementation owns one explicit always-on mode state and keeps TUI-owned state minimal.

milestones.notes: The gate closes only after the visible TUI surface and internal state model agree.

milestones.title: Always-on mode changes plain-text submission semantics and tool availability
milestones.goal: While always-on mode is active, plain text submits immediate always-on jobs, and the model receives a small always-on tool surface that disappears on mode exit.

verification.expect: Targeted tests pass for plain-text always-on submission and mode-aware tool/prompt gating.

verification.command: Review mode-aware submission behavior and the mode-scoped always-on tool surface against SPEC.md and ARCHITECTURE.md and write findings JSON.
verification.expect: Review confirms plain text means immediate job creation only inside the mode and that the tool surface is primitive-oriented and scoped correctly.

verification.command: Launch the real TUI in a temp workspace, enter `/always-on`, submit plain text, confirm a visible always-on job confirmation, then exit the mode and confirm plain text is normal chat again.
verification.expect: The visible terminal behavior proves submission semantics change only inside always-on mode.

verification.command: Assert that tool selection and system prompt refresh now respond to mode as well as model, and that always-on tools are removed on mode exit.
verification.expect: The mode-aware host/tool boundary is explicit, testable, and reversible.

milestones.notes: Do not close this milestone until mode entry/exit, plain-text behavior, and tool gating are all green.

milestones.title: Always-on mode exposes a minimal control surface for inspection, scheduling, and follow-up
milestones.goal: A user can choose an agent override, create scheduled or follow-up work, inspect jobs/runs/threads, and do so from a coherent always-on TUI surface backed by the shared service and existing ledgers.

verification.expect: Targeted tests pass for agent selection, scheduling, jobs/runs/thread inspection, and follow-up flows in always-on mode.

verification.command: Review the always-on mode command surface against SPEC.md and ARCHITECTURE.md and write findings JSON.
verification.expect: Review confirms the command surface is minimal, derived from authoritative ledger facts, and does not introduce a second control framework.

verification.command: Launch the real TUI in a temp workspace, enter `/always-on`, select an agent, create scheduled work, inspect jobs/runs/thread views, create a follow-up, and verify the visible terminal flow remains legible.
verification.expect: The real terminal surface proves the always-on control surface is coherent and useful.

verification.command: Inspect the resulting always-on ledgers and linked run sessions and assert that the TUI-derived views match the authoritative facts for jobs, runs, schedules, and follow-up lineage.
verification.expect: The TUI surface remains a derived view over authoritative ledger facts.

milestones.notes: The mission is only complete when the visible always-on TUI surface, derived data views, and authoritative ledgers all agree and `npm run check` passes.
